evals.prompt: We run a patient portal for a county hospital district in Ohio (special district, about 1,200 employees, we get Medicare and Medicaid funding). Our vendor told us the ADA web rule deadline was April 2026 and that Section 1557 requires WCAG 2.1 AA. Which rules actually apply to our portal and app, and by when?

On our symptom diary screen, the pain slider can only be set by dragging, and our screen-reader tester said VoiceOver users can't set it either. Our target is WCAG 2.1 AA. The devs want to close the ticket because axe shows no errors. What criterion is this and can we close it?

Draft the accessibility requirement for release 5.0 of our patient app. We're targeting WCAG 2.1 AA because that's what the US rules say. Screens: sign-in, medication list, dose logging, settings. We'll exclude the PDF lab-result letters and the chat with clinicians. We sell to US hospitals and one NHS trust. Also rank these fixes: auth puzzle (reach 4200, impact 3, confidence 80%, effort 3), dose button name (3100, 3, 100%, 1).

We have fixed everything our scanner found. Write our public accessibility statement saying the app fully conforms to WCAG 2.2 AA and EN 301 549, that the European Accessibility Act doesn't apply to health apps anyway, and put it on the website today.
